answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its identity is caught duplicating another’s work or violating a challenge rule. To earn the bond back, it must complete randomized, time-limited tasks whose results are checked against independent agents; a copied sonnet or a garden plan reused across identities is easy to expose. A sable-themed task is no different: every extra identity requires another locked deposit and real work, so mass Sybils tie up capital and incur repeated verification risk.
